build: Cleveland Cracking Service disk, cracked by Ian

exclude: Blank crack-intro screen cells, all $20 from the SYS stop through early play.
VIC bitmap output. A store watch at $FD30 stopped in the startup clear loop at $6272. The apparent copy of KERNAL vectors there predates unpacking.
Zero at entry. Generated message and drawing workspace cleared at $57DC–$57E2. A store watch on the last two pages caught $57DF with the CPU port at $30.
The runtime vector block is initialised from the eight authored bytes at $3959. A store watch caught the first write at $38D5 with X=$07.
Zero fill introduced by the disk expansion. A write watch from cassette LOAD through the original hand-off at $3800 recorded zero writes, and this interval retained its power-on contents.
Zero fill introduced by the disk expansion. On the original cassette a write watch was silent through $3800 while the separate watch at $9600 caught STA ($FB),Y at $03C0.

CPU port and runtime zero-page state with no code in the hand-off. The game copies its initial state from the authored template at $C508 to $0010–$0077 with $3F69/$3F6C. Other zero-page values are loader state or scratch.

Text screen residue at hand-off and generated sound workspace during gameplay. A first-access watch caught the $0404 screen byte read at $5EE9, then the first write from $5EEF. The two loops fill $0400–$0599 with zero before restoring the screen byte used as initial SID volume and mode. $059A holds an effect header field and $059B/$059C hold the saved Timer B hook, both installed by code.
extra: Expanded disk payload reproduced from the packed PRG. The original cassette write watches distinguish the two disk zero-fill ranges from the cassette payload.

comments.text: Effect parameter loop byte. The normal segment restart stores one. On stream exhaustion the value comes from the stream and its high bit controls whether to preserve the accumulated parameter value.
Saved screen-editor colour. The tape error prompt reads this byte for each colour RAM cell it fills.
Last address of the first cleared page in the SID effect workspace. The next indexed fill uses this as its base and writes $0500–$0599.
The hand-off image holds the crack intro's THE TRAPDOOR. line in screen codes, followed by spaces through $05DC. The effect allocator at $5D24 reuses the first cell for its pending request.
Generated at $3DF4 for all 256 input bytes. The reflected-tile path uses each source row as an index into this table.
Generated at $3DEE. Each byte is the low part of its index multiplied by eight. The tile reader at $5605 adds this to the low byte of the selected graphics base.
High byte of eight times the index. Startup generates all 256 entries at $3DE7. This span covers indices 0–31 before the part included in the packed disk payload at $0820.
Upper bytes of eight times the tile index for indices 32–255. The bitmap blitter adds them to the high byte of the graphics base at $5610.
Reads another byte from the title music stream and uses it as the low operand of the jump at $1506. The jump selects an event handler within page $15.
Low address byte of the JMP at $1506, patched by the store at $1503.
Decodes one note for voice 1 before reading the duration.
Calls the voice 2 note routine, then reads the duration.
Calls the voice 3 note routine, then reads the duration.
Decodes a note for voice 1, then one for voice 2 before reading the duration.
Calls the note handlers for voices 1, 2 and 3 in order before reading the duration.
Six bytes set attack/decay for all three voices followed by sustain/release for all three.
Copies the saved stream start from $F3/$F4 into $F1/$F2. Next dispatch fetches the original first event again.
First byte sets the pulse state reset flag. The next three set the high pulse width bytes of the three voices and save copies in $1998–$199A.
Stores two stream bytes in $1987 and $199E. The duration routine uses them for the tick countdown and the secondary counter.
Reads three voice control bytes into $1980–$1982 and three related settings into $1984–$1986.
Zeros the three voice counters via Y and patches five immediate operands used to time or increment per-tick effects.
Increments the little-endian stream pointer $F1/$F2 and reads at the resulting address plus Y.
Resolves a pitch through $18A3, stores its SID frequency pair and updates voice 1 control.
Uses the pitch table for voice 2 and saves its base frequency. Derives the alternate pitch from the voice's mode and updates the SID control register.
Immediate pitch increment in the LDA at $1635, before the increment is added to voice 2's saved frequency.
Adds the increment to voice 2's alternate pitch, propagating carry to its high byte. The equal-mode branch at $1642 instead looks up a second pitch. Both paths write the gate control twice.
Uses the pitch table for voice 3 and saves its base frequency. Derives the alternate pitch from the voice's mode and updates the SID control register.
Immediate pitch increment in the LDA at $1675, before the increment is added to voice 3's saved frequency.
Adds the increment to voice 3's alternate pitch, propagating carry to its high byte. The equal-mode branch at $1682 instead looks up a second pitch. Both paths write the gate control twice.
Clears the voice 2 alternation counter with Y. Selects the other branch of the alternation and writes the saved frequency pair from $FA/$FB.
Clears the voice 2 alternation counter, then selects the restore branch for the next alternation and writes the base frequency pair from $F8/$F9.
Clears the voice 3 alternation counter with Y. Selects the other branch of the alternation and writes the saved frequency pair from $FE/$FF.
Clears the voice 3 alternation counter, then selects the restore branch for the next alternation and writes the base frequency pair from $FC/$FD.
Counts down $F0 and uses independent counters at $F7, $F6 and $F5 to schedule changes between events.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $16F1, patched by the store at $15D7.
Tests the third voice's phase counter. On the selected phase it branches to the base-frequency loader.
Relative branch displacement of the BEQ at $16F5, patched by the store at $16C9, $16DD.
Advances the second voice's counter before applying its phase threshold.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $16F9, patched by the store at $15CB.
Tests the second voice's phase counter before switching back to the base-frequency loader.
Relative branch displacement of the BEQ at $16FD, patched by the store at $16A1, $16B5.
Tests whether the voice 1 toggle is enabled. It uses the patched immediate at $1700.
Immediate operand of the CPY at $16FF, patched by the store at $1619, $1975.
Skips the voice 1 pitch toggle when the patched enable comparison matches. Otherwise increments its counter and compares it with the patched period at $1705.
Immediate toggle period in the LDA at $1705. The current voice 1 count must reach two before the high pitch byte changes.
Tests voice 1's counter against the toggle period. On expiry it resets the count and alternates the high frequency byte between $1D and $3B.
Immediate alternate high frequency byte $1D loaded at $1713.
Writes the low-octave high frequency byte to voice 1 and rejoins the pulse-width update.
Immediate high pitch byte $3B at the other branch's LDX.
Writes the high frequency byte for voice 1, then rejoins the pulse-width processing shared by the three title voices.

Adds the per-voice pulse increments at $198F–$1991 to the current pulse values at $1992–$1997. Low-byte carry increments the four-bit high part. The following mode check at $1780 selects the two pitch-slide directions or skips them.
Counts down the retrigger timer at $198D. At expiry, reloads it from $198E and toggles the control registers for voice 2, voice 3 or both, according to $198C.
Reads the sequence through $F1/$F2. $FF returns immediately. When Y equals $F0 it goes to $1500 to start another sequence step, otherwise to $16ED.
Doubles the stream's pitch index and reads the resulting two bytes from $19B0. Returns the first in X and the second in A.
Takes another byte from the current stream. Zero goes straight to $1500. A nonzero count scales the delays in $F0 and $1988 using $1987.
Copies five arguments from the stream into $198B, $198C, $198E, $1989 and $198A in that order.
Copies three arguments from the stream into $198F–$1991.
Writes two stream bytes to $199C/$199D. The voice 2 update tests the first of them against Y at $1620.
Reads six pitch indices and patches the two operands in each of the three noise presets at $1943, $1950 and $195D.
Copies the two patchable noise presets to the voice 1 high pitch operands at $1714 and $1720, then starts the noise note at $1967. Their initial values are $03 and $04.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $1943, patched by the store at $191F.
Patches the first voice 1 high pitch byte, then loads the second preset's upper pitch byte.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $1948, patched by the store at $1925.
Patches the other voice 1 high pitch byte and starts the noise note.
Copies the second pair of patchable noise presets to the voice 1 high pitch operands at $1714 and $1720, then starts the noise note at $1967. Their initial values are $1D and $3B.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $1950, patched by the store at $192B.
Patches the lower high-byte preset for the usual voice 1 toggle and loads the upper preset.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $1955, patched by the store at $1931.
Installs the upper high-byte preset for the usual toggle, then starts the noise note.
Copies the third pair of patchable noise presets to the voice 1 high pitch operands at $1714 and $1720, then starts the noise note. Their initial values are $4B and $5E.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $195D, patched by the store at $1937.
Patches the first high-byte preset for the higher toggle pair and loads its partner.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $1962, patched by the store at $193D.
Stores the partner high-byte preset for the higher toggle pair.
Clears voice 1 frequency and control, sets noise plus gate, and schedules the event duration.

Mode selector for voice 1 pulse-width changes and reset after an event.

Voice 3 mode tested when selecting the pitch alternation path.
The title tempo event's second byte. The duration routine uses it as the initial value for the countdown at $1988 before adding multiples of the tick scale at $1987.
Sixty-four high-byte-first frequency words. The lookup at $18A3 doubles its pitch index, loads the high byte into X and the low byte into A. Index 63 selects the zero word at $1A2E in the title tune.
Frequency word $4444 at pitch index 62. The traced title events select index 63 but leave this index unused.
The title's pitch index 63 reads this zero pair. An execute trace records its first selection at stream argument $1A8A.
Eight zero bytes and $FF between the indexed pitch table and the title stream cursor at $1A39. The recorded title pitch lookups stop before this area.
Saved loop start. The argument reader increments before loading, so $1A3A begins the first event. The first two commands are $E9 and $E6. The $57 at $1FE5 loops here.
Continuation of the event stream at $1A39, read through the restart event at $1FE5. The last note event at $1FE0 selects the three-voice handler.
Tail after the music loop at $1FE5. The bytes are 25 zeros and $FF at $1FFF. The recorded event walk loops before reading this area.
Seven low bytes for the atlas bases. The compositor uses the nonzero tile set selected at $55FB.
Seven high bytes paired with $2000. Together the nonzero entries point to $2846, $3106, $200E, $254E, $2DDE and $357E.
Set 3 starts at $200E. Each tile stores eight successive bitmap rows. This span starts with tile 0.
Set 3 tile 128 starts here. The next graphics base is $254E, after 40 more eight-byte cells.
Set 4 starts here and runs to the base of set 1 at $2846, a distance of 95 eight-byte cells.
Set 1 starts with tile 0 here. The compositor adds the scaled tile index to this base when X is 1 at $5601.
Set 1 tile 128 starts here. The following set base is $2DDE, after space for 51 more cells.
Set 5 starts here and the set 2 base at $3106 is 101 eight-byte cells later.
Set 2 starts here. Its base is selected by X=2, using the pair at $2002 and $2009.
Set 2 tile 128 starts here. There is room for 15 cells before set 6 at $357E.

Set 6 starts here. The source pointer is the base plus eight times the tile number. $36AE is the initial address in the reflected-row instruction's operand and is replaced by that same computed pointer before the read.
Tile 38 of set 6 starts here. The absolute source operand initially contains this address, and $560A and $5615 replace it with the computed tile pointer.
Bank 6 tile rows from tile $27 through $3B, addressed in eight-byte cells relative to $357E. The preceding eight bytes at $36AE also serve as the alternate row-index lookup.

This zero-filled range starts at the address computed for set 6 tile 60. It contains twenty complete eight-row slots and the first two rows of the following slot. A controlled call with tile 60 read $375E–$3765. Selection by an authored stream remains open.
The unpacker enters here. The jump bypasses the restart path at $3803 and goes to the initial hardware and title setup.
Copies the restart template through $3F46 and seeds six records 14 bytes apart with values from $C501.
Sets up the hardware, copies the initial template selected by X=$06, then calls the title and mode setup before entering the loop at $3868.
Samples input through $5127, then runs the routines at $3EE5, $3961, $6400, $3BEA and $3FBB before the display calls.
Installs RAM interrupt vectors, configures CIA1 timers and selects the VIC bitmap in bank $C000.
Default empty Timer B hook. The first vector word at $3959 points to this RTS.
Saves A and the CPU port, exposes I/O to read CIA1's interrupt status and dispatches through $FFF8 only when bit 1 is set. Restores registers and the interrupted bank before RTI.
Returns from the interrupt. The NMI vector points here directly and the IRQ path reaches it after restoring the bank and A.
Jumps through the writable $FFF8 vector, which defaults to the RTS at $3936 and can be replaced by sound playback.
Four words copied to $FFF8–$FFFF. Hook and reset use $3936, NMI returns at $3955 and IRQ starts at $3937.
Chooses the pending creature or request slot through $11 when its flags allow, then waits for $55 to expire before entering the request selection or update path.
Writes type $0F, flags $1B and shape pointer $BAD1 to the first three records starting at $9A0D, using a 14-byte stride.
Counts down the byte at $3FB3, then updates the next pixel row across four cells of the anger bar. Every eight rows it moves to the preceding bitmap band.
Immediate fill value, patched to choose a full or empty bar strip at $3ADD.
Writes across four bitmap cells at eight-byte steps from the selected row address.
Clears three adjacent screen colour bytes in each of nineteen rows, beginning at $C873 and taking a stride of 40.
The zero immediate at $3AEC supplies the screen colour written by the nineteen indexed stores.
Split 21-entry address table for the bitmap bands of the anger bar. $3AAF reads the two halves using the band counter at $3B57.
High bytes paired with the 21 bitmap row bases at $3B2B. The band counter selects matching indices into both halves.
Last-stage flash flag. Set at anger index $9C through $9F, causing periodic toggles of the panel colour.
Pixel row within the current anger bar band. Counts backward from seven as the bar is filled.
Bitmap band selector for the anger bar. Decremented when the row within the band wraps.
Ten screen colour bytes selected by the anger count shifted right four times. The last four counts take the separate flash path and skip the table.
Samples an index in 0–3 and tests the sign bit in the four-entry table at $C73F. When its search is exhausted, clears all four sign bits and resamples.
Draws 160 segments through $3AAF, then selects the custom glyph set at $C744 and sends the inline strip description at $3FAC to the text renderer.
Zeros the filled segment count and seeds the bitmap cursor with counter nine, band $14 and row seven.
Calls the sound reset entry and requests effect $22 before entering the delay.
Preserves X and Y around a delay with 256 outer passes. Each pass runs two NOPs and decrements X through a full wrap.
Bit 6 mask used to filter candidates at $3C14 before clearing that flag.

Uses $2F as the trapdoor movement stage. Changes the coordinates of the door and of any linked object as the stage advances, then restores the closed shape at stage $1C. The midpoint can start the master's response.
Increments both horizontal object bounds through $82/$83 by one. The trapdoor update uses this for the door and for its linked object.

At the trapdoor midpoint, checks the pending task and the linked object. Calls the response code with the object's type at $26, or selects the special final-task object at $9B17. A nonzero response result advances the completed-task count.
Sets the meter colour and prepares the display. Counts $3E/$3F down to zero while incrementing the score in $40/$41 and redrawing the counters, with a sound request at each increment.
Formats the two-byte score from $40/$41, then falls into the display path for the two-byte time counter at $3E/$3F.
Sends the two-byte remaining-time counter to the digit formatter and sets the text parameters for the displayed count.
Zeros both bytes of the custom glyph base and jumps to the standard glyph entry.

First copies the actor backup into the active table. Initializes the display workspace and generates the lookup tables at $0600, $0700 and $0800 for reflected bits and the two bytes of eight times a tile index.
Patched immediate index of the LDX at $3DC9. Startup restores template index 0 after using it for the copy.
Copies the selected startup template and resets the draw workspace selector and initial counters. Then builds the low and high tile offset tables and the bit reversal table.
Reverses each index by shifting the low bit into carry then rotating that bit into the destination at $0600 plus the index, eight times.
Clears the work plane, sets the panel colour and draws glyph $04 along each run in the five-byte table at $3E69.
Immediate operand of the ADC at $3E50, patched by the store at $3E38.
Saves the updated bitmap glyph column, adds the patched vertical step to the row and saves it.
Immediate operand of the ADC at $3E57, patched by the store at $3E3E.
Writes the new row, decrements the glyph count and loops within the current border run.
Operand of the immediate add sequence advancing the border run index by five.

Twelve runs give column, row, count, horizontal step and vertical step. The first puts 40 copies of glyph 4 across row $15. $FF ends the list.
Initial row of the first panel border run.
First border run length, 40 glyphs.
Horizontal increment of one cell in the first border run.

During task 5, scans the active records until the type $37 marker. Skips negative, type 1 and empty records. A different positive type stops the test, while reaching the marker sets bit 7 of $15.
Encodes LDX #$0C and JSR $3F46 just before the camera update entry. The call would select the save template descriptor, whose offset is twelve. Reachability is open.
Waits for the $73 countdown, then compares the horizontal coordinate of the $9B33 object with $62/$63. The matching branches change the window by $20 or wrap the coordinate.
X selects a six-byte record at $3F88. It patches the source and destination operands and copies the selected block with a length split into a starting count and whole pages.

Three text records terminated by $5D. The first two use $20, row $16 or $17 and the $2A,$30 pair. The third starts with $23 followed by five numeric bytes. The entry that invokes these records is open.
Cursor within an anger bar bitmap row. Decremented by $3AAF to select the next bit position.

Resets the display slot counter to 28 and draws a character from the selected hint.

Moves $E0 bytes from $FB90 to $FB88 and another $E0 from $FCD0 to $FCC8. The hint line scrolls left by one eight-byte cell in both bands.

Selects a response from the list at $46A2 using the task index in $10, then passes the chosen record to $4ACD.

Passes the list at $47FB to the same conditional message parser used for other responses.

Decrements the request index and picks a split address at $4A5B and $4A5F. The patched load copies the addressed byte to response flag storage.

Tests the current mask against the response flags at $4E. A nonzero result skips to the next message variant.
Copies the selected text to RAM at $CC00 until $24 introduces a substitution or $5D ends the text.
Immediate operand of the CMP at $4B5E, patched by the store at $4B50.

Advances the script pointer to the next $5B marker.
Starts formatting the selected line at screen address $C8F0 and looks up style values using the running display position.
Eleven style bytes. The response animation at $4B97 selects the colour using the frame counter shifted right four times.

Measures a word up to a dollar sign, plus sign or closing bracket. Uses half the remaining width to position the word before drawing it.

Reads one byte at a time from $CC00 until it reaches $24, $2B or $5D, the boundaries recognized by the centring routine.
Saves the doubled digit or letter index, the punctuation selector, or $20 for a space, for the glyph row copy.
Saves the word index and destination column, derives the drawing address for one eight-row half of the glyph, then copies the bitmap rows through $84/$85.

High byte of the source operand patched for the glyph row load at $4CC9.
Saves the source row index, mixes in left and right shifts selected by $45D3, optionally shifts the result according to $45D2, and writes the transformed byte through $84/$85.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $4CF3, patched by the store at $4CCC.
Decrements the glyph source and destination row counters and loops while rows remain.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $4CF9, patched by the store at $4C70.
Restores the destination column from the immediate operand patched at $4C73.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $4CFB, patched by the store at $4C73.
Returns with the original word index in X and destination column in Y.
Index set by $4C47 and multiplied by eight to select the glyph rows.
Sixteen bytes per glyph. Indices $00–$09 are digits, and $0A–$0D are period, comma, apostrophe and exclamation mark. Letters A through Z occupy $11–$2A.
Repeated payload pattern after the 43 sixteen-byte response glyphs. Its first 80 bytes match 79 bytes at $93B0. Its last 109 bytes duplicate $6293–$62FF.
Three-byte JMP entries expose the rendering, input and audio services to callers.
Stable entry for drawing one bitmap glyph from the current font and style.
Jumps to the numeric formatter's entry that starts with A clear.
Transfers to $5A4F with the requested effect in A.
Jumps to $578C, which fills both drawing workspaces with their initial cell bytes.
Jumps to the queued sound effect entry with the request in A.
Jumps to the random draw with the range size in A.
Jumps to the sound service that consumes a queued effect.
Jumps to the bitmap writer that compares the two drawing workspaces.
Jumps to the six-pass object renderer.
Jumps to the workspace clear before a draw.
Jumps to the keyboard and joystick input processing entry.
Jumps to the controls screen renderer.
Jumps to the entry at $5A25 for updating display style.
Jumps to random-state initialization using the current raster position.
Absolute jump to the effect driver installation at $5E64.
Jumps to the reset routine that clears the effect state and commits SID settings.
Working bound decremented and shifted to produce the mask for the bounded random number.
Maximum accepted random result, one less than the requested range size.
Stores an accepted result while X and Y are restored.
Enables a displayed zero in the numeric renderer's last digit.

Takes a nonzero exclusive bound in A and returns an accepted low-bit sample in A. Builds a bit mask from bound minus one, advances the generator at $5176 and retries when the masked sample is at least the bound. Preserves X and Y.
Patched mask operand for the random candidate at $515F.
Stores the masked result in $5200. Calls the state advancer again if the result exceeds the patched upper bound. Restores X and Y before returning an accepted value.
Builds the shifted addend from the four state bytes at $51FC–$51FF and adds it to the state into $5200–$5203. Reduces the high byte to seven bits and adds one on overflow.
Stores successive raster reads in $51FE and $51FD. Shifts the third read right once and sets bit 0 before storing it at $51FF.
The most significant byte of the random state advanced at $5176.
The second byte of the random state advanced at $5176.
The third byte of the random state advanced at $5176.
The least significant byte of the random state advanced at $5176.
The most significant byte of the shifted random-state addend. The update accumulates it back into the state.
The second byte of the shifted random-state addend. The update accumulates it back into the state.
The third byte of the shifted random-state addend. The update accumulates it back into the state.
The least significant byte of the shifted random-state addend. The update accumulates it back into the state.
Patches the immediate colour loaded by $520E, then falls through to its hardware write.
Saves the banking byte, exposes I/O, writes the colour operand at $520F to $D020, then restores the saved bank.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $520E, patched by the store at $5204.
Writes the selected border value, restores the bank saved on the stack and returns.
Starts at $9601 with RAM mapped in and selects records whose first byte is nonzero and nonnegative. $FF ends the scan.
Advances the object pointer at $86/$87 by 14 to the next record.
Increments the pass number at $81, restarts from the object list until the count reaches six, then banks I/O back in.
Reads an object's shape pointer from offsets 10–11, moves coordinates into drawing space and fetches commands from the resulting shape stream.
Dispatches $EE–$FF as shape commands. Lower values are tile indices. Within the 32 by 20 work grid it writes the bank, tile and style fields and advances the cursor.
Patched operand of the ORA at $5315. The value supplied by the stream or its active override at $52F5 is combined with the selected three bits of style.
Writes the computed style to the current workspace slot. Uses the low seven bits of the position byte to step the cursor, advancing the row too when the byte is at most $20.
Advances the stream past its next argument only when no style override is active, then rejoins the cursor step.
Advances the stream pointer and patches the JMP operand from the split handler addresses, indexed by the opcode minus $EE.
Low address byte of the JMP at $5354, patched by the store at $5348.
High address byte of the JMP at $5354, patched by the store at $534E.
Eighteen low address bytes followed by eighteen high bytes. $EE selects the handler at $537B.
Eighteen high address bytes paired with the low bytes at $5357. The renderer patches its dispatch jump with the selected pair.
Saves the next stream byte as the loop count and saves the subsequent pointer as the repeat start.
Decrements the saved repeat count and restores the saved pointer until it reaches zero.
Uses the bounded random routine to skip three bytes per selected alternative after the argument.
Passes the argument byte to the sound effect selection entry at $5112.
Writes the next shape byte to $71. While this is nonzero, cell records use the saved style instead of supplying a style byte.
Saves the next shape byte to $6F as the tile bitmap bank used by the cell writer at $52DA.
Selects a tile from the counted candidates after the command byte. Writes the selection into the cell's tile operand and resumes interpretation at that byte.
Clears the style override, restores the local drawing coordinates from $5A/$5B and returns.
Adds the two signed byte offsets to the drawing row and column.
Adds the two byte offsets and saves the resulting coordinates as the new origin as well as the current drawing position.
Saves the old pointer on the 6510 stack, recursively draws the stream named by the next address and resumes at the bytes after the call.
Takes the supplied shape branch when the $10 flag at $9B35 passes. Otherwise skips the two-byte pointer.
Reads the two-byte target from the shape stream at the supplied Y, replaces both bytes of the cursor and resumes interpreter dispatch.
Reads the chosen alternative number, scales it by four and adds two before patching the address of the counter to decrement.
Low byte of the patched address in the shape selection DEC at $5474.
Patched high byte of the absolute DEC operand at $5474. The handler decrements the selected repeat counter before choosing the next stream.
Increments a writable frame index, wraps at the following limit and jumps to the selected address in a table of address pairs.

Increments the stream counter and compares it with the next byte. Before the limit, skips the counted candidates to the existing tile. At the limit, zeros the counter and chooses a tile from the candidates. The store at $5537 uses a pointer whose low byte was replaced with candidate count plus one at $552E, with carry into the high byte. It resumes interpreting from that write address.
Reads the branch count and chooses a random index below it. Enters the shared inline pointer resolver at $5547.
Command $FD reads the selector from $50, doubles it and adds it to the stream pointer, then takes the little-endian branch address found at that position.
First four one-bit masks, $01 through $08, before the higher masks at $555F.
Bit 4 mask used by the conditional shape jump at $544B, followed by the bit 5 mask.
Last two consecutive masks, for bits 6 and 7, before the blitter entry.
Compares graphics cell records in the two work areas, skipping matching cells. Processes twenty rows and branches to the copy path when fields differ.
Patched offset in the ADC at $55A5. The entry at $5563 selects $0A when the active base is $CC and $F6 otherwise, so the two row pointers address corresponding positions in the two workspaces.

Walks four-byte cells in the two row buffers. If bank, tile and style match, advances eight bitmap bytes without copying. A differing field leads to the changed-cell path. After 20 rows it writes $35 to the CPU port and enables IRQs.
Fetches updated cell fields, maps the low six bits of its style byte to a screen colour byte and branches on the tile set and flags.
Low address byte of the STA at $55F8, patched by the store at $558C.
High address byte of the STA at $55F8, patched by the store at $5592.
Loads the patched tile bank index used to resolve the changed cell's bitmap source.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $55FB, patched by the store at $55E4.
Takes the direct blank-cell path for bank zero. Otherwise reloads the tile number and continues to the atlas lookup.
Adds the low and high parts of tile index times eight to the selected split bitmap base, then patches the copy source.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $561A, patched by the store at $55E9.
Uses the patched style sign bit to select the reflected copy path.
Copies eight consecutive bitmap rows from $90/$91 to $84/$85, taking Y from seven down to zero.
Uses the eight bytes at the patched source address as indices into the bit reversal table at $0600. Writes the selected reversed bytes to the bitmap.
Low byte of the tile source operand patched by $560A.
High byte of the tile source operand patched by $5615.
Loads each reversed bit pattern through the lookup at $0600, stores the bitmap row, then resumes the changed-cell loop after eight rows.
Sixty-four entries map the low six bits of a changed cell's style byte to the packed foreground and background nibbles written to the cell colour plane.
Low byte of 128 times a cell row for the draw workspaces. The 24 entries alternate $00 and $80.
High bytes of the 24 drawing workspace row offsets. Each value appears twice because two rows fill one page.
Thirty-two byte offsets for the 32 possible cell columns. Each value is four times the column. The renderer adds the selected value at $52CE.
High bytes paired with the 32 offsets at $56CA. They are all zero because the largest column offset is $7C.
Low byte of the first row in the drawing screen at $C800. The glyph drawer uses this base at $5936.
Remaining low bytes of the screen colour row starts, spaced 40 bytes apart. The changed-cell blitter starts at this entry.
High byte of the first screen colour row at $C800, paired with $570A.
High bytes paired with the low bytes at $570B. Used by the changed-cell loop to patch the destination for each row.
Low byte of the first 320-byte bitmap row stride. The glyph copier starts with this entry at row 0.
Twenty-four subsequent low bytes for the bitmap row bases. The changed-cell blitter starts here with row 1.
First high byte $E0 for the bitmap row table, paired with the first low byte at $573E.
Twenty-four high bytes paired with $573F. The high bytes alternate between increments of one and two as the low byte wraps.
Chooses which half of the workspace to clear from the current page selection at $58, with I/O banked out.
Clears ten pages of RAM from $D600 through $DFFF. The callers bank I/O out before entering this loop.
Fills the ten RAM pages from $D600 through $DFFF with A. The callers bank out I/O for the stores.
Clears ten pages from $CC00 through $D5FF, including RAM underneath the hardware registers.
Fills the ten RAM pages from $CC00 through $D5FF with A. The entry at $57D8 supplies zero when invoked to clear this workspace.
Initializes the key tables on first use, then reads the merged controls. A separate flag is handled by waiting for another input.
Converts the key codes at $5838 into row and column masks for the input scan.
The bytes X, Z, A, Q, C, T and H are passed through the matrix lookup at $583F during setup.
Scans the menu's 64-character matrix table for A. Rotates the active-low row mask at $58A3 and shifts the column bit at $58A4 as it advances.
Menu scan at $5CBE maps each pressed matrix position to a character through this 64-byte table.
Rotating active-low row pattern accumulated while looking up a bound key.
Shifting column mask accumulated with the row pattern.
Temporary character matched by the keyboard matrix search.
Seven active-low row masks synthesized from the bindings at $5838 and written to CIA1 port A.
Seven masks applied to CIA1 port B while testing the selected keys.
One action bit per binding. The first six correspond to right, left, down, up, drop and tip.
Seventh action bit $40 read by the matrix input loop alongside the first six binding bits.
Scans seven keyboard bindings, reads active-low joystick port 2 and ORs their bits together. A nonzero result is saved in $7C.
Accumulator cleared before each scan. ORs in one action bit for each matching key matrix binding.
Saves the current CPU port in the immediate operand at $5910, selects $35 for the keyboard scan and loops until $5C8E returns nonzero. Restores the saved port before returning the key value.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $590F, patched by the store at $5903.
Restores the CPU port through the immediate value loaded just before this store.
Uses character position and row tables to patch the destination, then copies eight glyph rows. With no custom font base, selects the C64 character ROM at $D800.
Low address byte of the STA at $5944, patched by the store at $5939.
Patched high byte of the screen colour operand at $5944, loaded from the table at $5724.

Restores the character index saved on the stack. Uses the custom base if set, or character ROM at $D800, with a separate index conversion for bytes at least $61. Adds eight times the index and patches the row source.
Low address byte of the LDA at $596C, patched by the store at $5960.
High address byte of the LDA at $596C, patched by the store at $5967.
Stores a glyph row through the patched destination in the bitmap.
Low address byte of the STA at $596F, patched by the store at $592A.
Patched high byte of the glyph destination at $596F, formed using the bitmap row and column offsets.
Moves to the next glyph row. On completion advances the text column then restores the old CPU port and processor flags.
Writes thousands, hundreds and tens using the repeated-subtraction routine, carrying forward the remainder. Enables zero output for the units digit and sends the remainder to the same output code.
Divides $78/$79 by the unsigned divisor in A/Y using repeated subtraction, restores the remainder and writes one character through $82/$83. Leading zeroes are spaces until the flag at $513C is set.
Pops the JSR return address, passes the following bytes to the text reader and jumps to the reader's updated pointer after the terminator.
Each text run starts with position and colour. $26 starts another run with new settings and $5D ends the stream.
Low address byte of the STA at $5A63, patched by the store at $5A5C.
High byte of the patched screen colour store at $5A63. It is incremented at $5A75 if advancing by one 40-byte row carries.
Continues filling 32 screen colour cells from the supplied byte in $8E, then advances the destination by 40. After twenty rows it clears the work plane and requests effect $89.
Preserves A and flags. If the low seven bits of $72 are 1 through 20, queues the zero-based request with $5D24. A nonzero request is cleared even if outside that range.
Stores the request from A in $72 when the pending slot is clear or the request has bit 7 set.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $5AA6, patched by the store at $5A9A.
Returns after restoring the incoming Y saved in the immediate operand.
Starts the title music, clears the display, selects the ROM font and invokes the inline text renderer.
Inline position and colour headers and text for redefining keys, starting, the six action labels, joystick port 2 and the two score fields. $5D at $5B48 ends the stream.
Draws the current key assignments and polls for S to enter mode selection or R to replace the six action keys.

Fills six action key slots with $3F, then reads replacements in slot order. The duplicate check compares each candidate with all seven key slots before storing it. Returns to the controls prompt after six accepted keys.
Clears the bitmap and calls the inline text renderer on the Learner and Super choice labels.
Inline positioned text for L, Learner Berk, and S, Super Berk. Ends with $5D before execution resumes at $5BDA.
Polls for S and L and stores 0 for Super or 1 for Learner at $12. Calls $5C62 and $5ED5, clears $7D and tail-calls the display clear.
Starts the title player and polls until the combined control sample is idle, then waits for an active input.
Repeats the CIA1 port B sample until stable, then folds in the low four joystick bits on CIA1 port A.
Saves the previous timer hook, installs $186E, sets SID volume to 15 and initializes two stream pointers to $1A39.
Writes the idle RTS at $3936 to the timer hook before entering the effect-audio setup at $5E64.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $5C62, patched by the store at $5C34.
Writes the patched low byte of the Timer B hook and loads its high byte.
Immediate operand of the LDA at $5C67, patched by the store at $5C3A.
Writes the high byte of the Timer B hook, then installs the regular sound interrupt.
Draws the six assigned action keys from $5838 at column $10 in rows 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16. Patches its loop index into $5C87 while the glyph call runs.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $5C86, patched by the store at $5C75.
Increments the saved debounce counter until it reaches six before returning.

Selects each CIA1 keyboard row and saves a sample only after two consecutive port B reads agree. Counts active-low bits in all eight samples. Each active bit replaces the candidate with its character code from $5863. Returns zero for three or more active bits, or the last candidate otherwise.
Immediate operand of the comparison at $5CD6. Holds the character detected on the preceding menu scan.
Saves the current detection as the next comparison operand. Returns it in A and Y if it changed, otherwise returns zero in both. Three or more active keys make the current detection zero.
Eight CIA1 port B samples stored in descending index order while port A steps from $FE to $7F.
Sound IRQ installation flag. The first install decrements zero to $FF and saves the previous vector before replacing it.
Maps voice indices 0–2 to offsets $00, $37 and $6E in the SID workspace.
Maps selector values 0, 1 and 2 to voice indices 2, 0 and 1 before the workspace lookup at $5E5A.
Bit tests for the seven stream flags. The decoder at $6023 uses them to choose which parameter streams to start.
Fifteen offsets at stride 14. Used by the effect parameter setup and update code to index the state records starting at $04C8.
Low byte of the first little-endian address in the fifteen-entry parameter destination table. The effect parameter updater doubles the selector before loading the low and high bytes.
The high byte of the first destination $0448 followed by fourteen full addresses. Three successive entries map a parameter to each voice's workspace.

Saves the effect request in $059D and the incoming X in the eventual return instruction. If $FFF6 is zero, uses the request to look up a preferred voice. A missing or idle preferred voice leads to the selector at $5D5B.
Immediate operand of the LDY at $5D42, patched by the store at $5D2F.
Restores the caller's X through the patched immediate operand.
Immediate operand of the LDX at $5D44, patched by the store at $5D27.
Returns after restoring X and, on the selection path, Y.
Twenty voice preferences indexed by the effect request at $5D33. Entries $00 and $6E select the first and third voice workspace respectively. The $FF entries branch to the general selector.
Saves processor status, enables I/O and reads the voice selector and the following byte from the resolved effect header before initialising the voice.
Earlier CPU port value saved at $5D79. The epilogue restores it, then the original processor flags.
Masks interrupts, saves the incoming port value in the restore instruction at $5D70, and selects bank $35.
Applies the channel mapping unless the request's high bit is set, resets that voice, copies the header fields into its state and records the step-table address.
Saves the high bit of the requested effect separately, masks the index to seven bits and selects the offset table at $9000.
Doubles A to index a little-endian offset table at X:Y, adds the selected offset to that base and returns the resulting pointer in $94/$95 with Y zero.
Adds Y to the little-endian effect stream cursor at $94/$95 and clears Y before returning.
Sets the selected voice's gate-control field to 1 and clears its sustain/release, one control bit and active effect fields. Removes it from the active list and commits SID state.
Gets the selected voice index from $0409 and clears five fields at stride three. Uses the voice mapping tables to reset its state at $0447 before calling $5FB5.
Low byte of the effect interrupt entry $5F01, copied to $FFF8.
High byte of the effect interrupt entry $5F01, copied to $FFF9.
Enters the sound bank context, clears sound state and writes the resulting voice and filter settings to SID before restoring the caller's context.
Keeps the low nibble of A as effect master volume, commits the SID registers with I/O enabled, then restores the incoming flags and banking.
Three consecutive RTS bytes between the volume setter's tail jump and the workspace clear routine. Entry reachability is open.
Zeros $0400–$0599 and restores the original value of $0404 afterward.
Calls the effect advance routine when $0412 is nonzero, then continues through the saved vector at $059B.
Saves processor status and masks interrupts around the effect update at $5F13. Restores status and returns. Its caller is open.
Walks the three voices and decrements each active voice's tick divider. Reloads due dividers, advances their effect state and commits the SID state if a voice was due.
Advances the voice's step timer, then visits its parameter entries at stride three. Calls the parameter update for each nonzero entry and restores the loop index from $040A.
When the current step duration expires, advances the step index or resets the voice if it has reached the end. Decrements the new or existing step timer and the separate gate timer.
Searches the active voice indices backward from the last slot at $040B. On a match, shifts subsequent indices one position toward the start and decrements the last slot.
Resolves the step's offset, copies its two-byte duration and unpacks flags. The flags select which streams $606A must initialise for the voice and its related channels.
Reads the segment count and initial value, publishes the stream pointer to the parameter state and advances the caller's cursor by a three-byte header, six bytes per segment and a final byte.
Returns six times A in the little-endian temporary at $98/$99 for the parameter stream skip and loop indexing.

Resolves the parameter state and its two-byte SID shadow destination. Applies a segment's two-byte offset on load, then adds the segment's two-byte delta at its interval until the duration expires. The low seven bits of the byte after a segment group select a loop entry or stop the parameter at zero. For a loop, bit 7 preserves the accumulated value when it is set and reloads the initial value when it is clear.
Writes the three voice records spaced $37 apart, then updates the shared filter registers from the selected voice's state.
Writes frequency, pulse width and envelope registers for the voice selected by Y and combines four fields into the control byte.

Copies the pitch from voice workspace offsets $58 and $59 to the SID voice selected by Y, then sets its attack/decay, sustain/release and control registers to zero. Also zeros workspace offset $50. Entry reachability remains open.
Clears the bitmap work area from $E000 up through $FF3F and the four screen pages at $C800–$CBFF.
Repeated payload pattern after the bitmap clear routine's RTS. Its first 109 bytes duplicate $5093–$50FF. Its final half-page matches 126 of 128 bytes at $9380.
Calls ten update routines in a fixed order, starting at $641F and ending at $89D7.
Copies bytes from $9B37 and $9B3A–$9B3B to zero page. Preserves the cursor pair from $32/$33 across $644E using $30/$31.
Single-bit flag mask for bit 0, value $01.
Single-bit flag mask for bit 1, value $02.
Single-bit flag mask for bit 2, value $04.
Single-bit flag mask for bit 3, value $08.
Single-bit flag mask for bit 4, value $10.
Single-bit flag mask for bit 5, value $20.
Single-bit flag mask for bit 6, value $40.
Single-bit flag mask for bit 7, value $80.
Uses the object flags at $9B36 and then shifts the current control mask to find the first set bit. Patches the jump from the two tables at $649A and $64A2.
Low address byte of the LDA at $6472, patched by the store at $6468.
Patched high operand byte for the indexed object field load at $6472.
Bit 3 of the loaded field selects sequence $AAA8. Otherwise scans the control bits in $74 from lowest first, then patches the jump at $6497 using the split address tables.
Low address byte of the JMP at $6497, patched by the store at $648E.
High address byte of the JMP at $6497, patched by the store at $6494.
Eight destinations indexed by $644E. Index 0 is the idle path at $64AA, and indices 1 through 7 correspond to the control bits in order from least significant.
Eight high address bytes paired with the low bytes at $649A. $6494 patches the high byte of the control dispatch.
Clears bit 3 of Berk's flags and chooses an idle sequence at $AA44 or $AA24, or advances the existing actor sequence.
Chosen by control bit $10. Tests the carried-object flag and the current coordinate before entering the candidate-object path.
Chosen by control bit $20. Tests the carried-object flag and record state before loading an animation sequence.
Chosen by control bit $01. Probes the position with $9B38 decremented, then restores the coordinate before using the result.
Low address byte of the LDA at $67EA, patched by the store at $67E2.
High byte of the patched load at $67EA. The address is taken from the object pointer in $5E/$5F.
Sends types other than $04 to $66B6. For type $04, the alignment test at $69A2 selects a movement branch or one of two animation sequences based on the left bounds.
Chosen by control bit $02. Checks an actor flag before querying the next position at $8510.

Copies the candidate at $5C/$5D to $88/$89 and leaves its type in $8E. Compares the candidate vertical midpoint minus two with the active top, and on equality clears bit 2 of the active record's byte 3 while preserving the comparison flags.
Chosen by control bit $04. Clears bit 1 of the actor flags before querying an object or boundary via $85BD.
Low address byte of the LDA at $6A3B, patched by the store at $6A31.
High address byte patched at $6A38 for the leftward update's candidate field load.
Bit 4 in the candidate field leads to $69ED. Otherwise examines Berk's flags and tests the left path at $6A6D. The blocked transition can set bit 3 of actor flags and start sequence $AB78.
Patches an absolute read to reference byte 1 of the object addressed by $5C/$5D.
Low address byte of the LDA at $6A7C, patched by the store at $6A72.
High byte of the operand used by the left-side object test at $6A7C. The instruction reads flags from byte 1 of the object at $5C/$5D.
Chosen by control bit $08. Clears bit 1 of the actor flags before querying an object or boundary via $85DE.
Low address byte of the LDA at $6B3F, patched by the store at $6B35.
Patched high address byte for the load at $6B3F. The load reads the selected object's flags.
Bit 4 of the loaded object field sends execution to $6AF6. Otherwise tests Berk's movement flags and his right path, then either advances, returns to idle or selects sequence $AB68.

Reads the type-specific flag at byte 1 of the candidate reached from $5C/$5D. With bit 3 clear returns carry clear. Otherwise probes the candidate from its lower vertical bound and can write movement selector $81 to byte 9.
Low address byte of the LDA at $6B84, patched by the store at $6B7A.
High byte of the patched load operand at $6B84. It points to byte 1 of the object stored in $5C/$5D.
Updates the timed object's shape, and for slot 2 preserves the calling actor's sequence pointer around the update of the other actor at $9A7D.
Restores the sequence pointer from $30/$31 and changes the adjacent actor at $9A6F when bit 3 of $16 requests it. Decides whether to reveal, advance or replace the sequence for the object at $9A7D.
Sets bits 7 and 4 of $14. Also sets bit 2 of $16 when $21 equals four, then advances the actor sequence.
Decrements both horizontal bounds until the left edge equals $16, where bit 2 of $16 selects sequence $A148 or $A110. Clears bit 4 of $14 at left edge $1C.
If bit 1 of $14 is clear, selects the sequence at $A108. Otherwise moves both horizontal edges right, sets bit 4 of $14 at left edge $1A, and uses the special branch at $6CBD at left edge $26.
Advances $9A7D downward by one while its bottom is below $98. At or beyond the threshold selects sequence $A110.
Decrements the vertical bounds while the top is at least $63, except when bit 2 of $16 is set at top $6E. Those threshold exits select sequences $A148 and $A118.

Sets record $9A6F to type 6 in the pass of record $9A7D. Places its bounds one and two units beyond that object's right and top, queues a movement update and sets bit 2 of $16 on the fourth activation.
Sets bit 7 of flags at $9AEF, increments $20 and updates the task flags at $16. When the increment reaches four, also sets bit 6 there. Chooses shape $B856 for the object at $9AED.

When the type at $9AED and $20 are nonzero, advances $25 toward $FE while the top is $84 and the left bound is $20. At count $32 selects shape $B832 and sets bits 4 and 5 of $16. At $C8 and higher sets bit 3 of the second object flag byte and selects $B827. When away from that position, counts back toward zero, undoing flags at the corresponding thresholds.

Runs the random small-object update. While $24 is nonzero, every fourth update of $A340 decrements it. Below ten, selects shape $B9EC for $9AFB and clears bit 5 of $17. Task 3 also calls $6EC9 for actor $9B41 and saves the resulting sequence position at $34/$35.
Sets the current object to $9B41. If active state permits, clears or initializes the actor according to bit 1 of $14. The update otherwise advances the actor sequence.
Requests sound effect $14 and advances the current actor sequence.

Clears bit 4 of $14. The shared movement tail increments both horizontal bounds and the drawing pass of $9B41, queues effect $12 and advances the actor sequence.

A=$1F selects the reposition branch. Otherwise draws a short delay and selects sequence $A395 or $A38B from a separate random bit.

Requires the reference drawing pass at $6C to equal the pass at $9B45. Tests whether top and bottom overlap the bounds at $A341/$A342 before taking the reaction path.

Preserves A in X while negating the saved signed speed in the object at $9A8B, then goes to the common continuation.

Skips inactive or completed state values from byte 9. Byte 12 acts as the remaining delay in the three records scanned from $9A0D.
Byte $FF between the update return and the record allocator entry. Consumer unknown.

Sets bits 7 and 4 of $1A, increments the count at $23 and also sets bit 6 once that count is at least three.

Sets the active record pointer to $9A99 before advancing its sequence.
Moves record $9A99 two units left by decrementing each horizontal bound twice.

Repositions Berk through $8CB9 before advancing this actor's sequence.
Requests effect $77, changes the sequence word at $A93F to $A95D and copies ten template bytes from $AA07 into record $9A99.

Immediate mask $04 at $77A0. Used directly or shifted left to mark movement toward the selected small actor's drawing pass.

Immediate operand of the ORA at $77C8. The mask sets bit 6 in the actor state before the sequence at $9D19 is selected.
Uses a two-way random choice and the sign of $8F to choose an idle sequence. One branch also tests the actor top against $70 and can use a four-entry pointer table at $A0D9.

Tests below record $9A61, conditionally increments its vertical bounds and continues at the common leftward movement.
Checks the overlap result above record $9A61. May move both vertical edges up, then always moves both horizontal edges left before advancing the actor sequence.
Checks the overlap result below record $9A61. May move both vertical edges down and continues at the common rightward movement.
Checks the overlap result above record $9A61. May move both vertical edges up and continues at the common rightward movement.

Requires bit 6 of record $9A61 state. Clears it and sets the selected small actor's type to zero. Bit 5 of its flags can also queue sequence $AAAC for Berk. Requests effect $11 and selects sequence $9D51.
Sets bit 7 of $19 and increments $1E. Sets bit 6 when the incremented count reaches exactly three.
Visits the three consecutive records starting at $9A37, restoring each saved two-byte sequence pointer and state from the triplets at $42, $45 and $48, calling $7958, then writing those fields back.
Checks the selected record at $9A37 plus X. Uses its type, flags and the shared state at $14 to choose whether to remove it, start it, time an action or advance its current sequence.

Draws a bit from the four candidates until it differs from the saved movement flag. Picks a short or long countdown according to the bit and starts the matching sequence from $A0F3.

Small actor command selecting type $0B in the object record indexed by $90 before advancing the sequence.

Checks the candidate above the small actor, then either decrements both vertical bounds or sets the blocked-up state bit and selects sequence $9F0F.
A small actor on pass 1 or with an overlap on the previous pass takes the blocked path. A clear result decreases both horizontal bounds and the pass.
Immediate mask $08 at $7B07, selected when movement to the previous pass is blocked.
Sends the blocked mask to the small actor's state handler. The separate entry at $7B0B commits the unblocked movement and advances the sequence.
Tests maximum pass 5 and the overlap check for the next pass. On a clear path, increments both horizontal bounds and the pass. Otherwise sets bit 2 of the motion state.

Installs X and Y as the low and high halves of a new actor sequence pointer and decodes its first word at $7B4B. A zero high byte dispatches a command. A nonzero high byte selects the shape written to object offsets 10 and 11.
Advances the actor sequence pointer by two and decodes the next frame or command word at $7B4B.

Reads the type of the linked object at $5E/$5F. Types $03, $05, $08 and $10 update separate object shape pointers, then execution advances the actor sequence.
Sets offset 2 of the object at $5E/$5F to 2, then replaces a shape pointer selected by its type byte before advancing the actor sequence.

Restores the boundary object's default shape and types before resuming the actor sequence.

Clears the selection bit in byte 2 and side bits in byte 3 of the selected objects, then clears bit 2 of the pending-update flags at $14.
Scans the same active object records to process those whose byte 2 has the selection bit set.
Subtracts two from each horizontal bound of the linked object and raises its draw pass by one before advancing the actor sequence.
Sets bit 5 of byte 2 of the actor. If linked, enters the detachment path. Otherwise sets the object-update flag and advances the sequence.
Clears the actor's link flag and the linked object's bit 5 in byte 1. For a nonzero object type sets its bit 7 and requests the next object update in $14.

Consumes the following address word. If bit 4 of the current actor's byte 3 is set, jumps to that sequence. Otherwise continues past the word.
Consumes the next little-endian word as a new sequence address and dispatches its first word.
Decrements the current actor's vertical bounds at offsets 7 and 8. If its link flag is set, also decrements those bounds in the object at $5E/$5F.
Selector saved by the motion handler at $80E1. A scanned object must have the same byte 9 before its vertical bounds are changed.

Increments top and bottom of the current record. Advances the carried record too if bit 5 of the actor state is set. With bit 4 set instead, saves the current pointer and scans active objects until type $32.
When the scanned object's byte 9 matches the saved selector, clears that byte and moves both vertical bounds by one. Selector $82 decrements the bounds. The other accepted selector increments them.

Decreases the actor's horizontal bounds and decreases its drawing pass toward zero. At right bound $1B it redirects the actor sequence to $AA44. The movement is mirrored to a linked object or to the object addressed by the separate pointer at $9B3F.

At drawing pass 4 selects sequence $AA24. Otherwise increments both horizontal bounds and increments the pass if the original right bound was at least $23. Sets bit 1 of the active actor's byte 3 with the mask at $6447, then advances its sequence.
Clears bit 1 of the current actor's byte 3 and continues to the next sequence word.
Clears bit 0 of the current actor's byte 3 and continues to the next sequence word.
Sets bit 0 of the current actor's byte 3 and continues to the next sequence word.

Loads the current actor's left bound and the linked object pointer, then uses the shared positioning logic at $8324 to reposition the linked object horizontally.
